marks.q: This excellent start, combined with the Group's strong financial footing, technology, capabilities, engineering specialisms, and its sector penetration in areas which are political priorities …… mean the Board is confident that the Group is well placed to deliver continued growth.

The strong start to the year, record open order book and trading momentum underpin the near-term prospects and give the Directors optimism for the outturn being at least in-line with analyst expectations and exciting midterm future prospects.

The strong trading …… means the Company expects to exceed the current revenue expectations and be marginally ahead of the adjusted PBT consensus expectations for FY23, despite the expected increase in interest charges.

The Board is confident of exceeding previous expectations for the year ending 31 March 2023. Whilst there is still some uncertainty as to potential impacts of component shortages and lead times, there is potential further upside in the second half.
The Board is pleased to report continued strong trading in the second half of the year, resulting in a performance for the Period that is at least in line with consensus expectations.

…… the strength of the order book, balanced with the investments made and planned, means pleasingly we expect revenue in FY2023/24 to be ahead of current consensus …… and adjusted profit before tax to be slightly ahead of current consensus.

The Board is confident in meeting the recently upgraded forecasts for the full year and in managing supply chain and input cost risks which remain stubborn, whilst also being mindful of the current macro-economic risks.

…… the Directors expect to deliver stronger than anticipated organic revenue growth, meaning the Group is expected to be marginally ahead of current consensus revenue and adjusted PBT expectations for the year ending 31 March 2024.
Robust orderbook of £108.6m at 31 October 2023 combined with a strong prospect pipeline, gives the Directors confidence in meeting full year consensus analyst expectations.

Revenues and adjusted profit before tax are expected to be ahead of consensus …… on deliveries …… previously expected to be recognised in FY25. The acceleration of revenues into the current year is reflected commensurately in the updated expectations for FY25.

Trading in FY24/25 is not expected to be first-half weighted as it was in FY23/24. However, pleasingly, year-to-date trading has been broadly in line with management expectations, which supports management confidence over the full year expectations.

Management expects (based upon the visible order pipeline) that orders, particularly from the defence sector, will be secured and delivered in the second half of the year to enable the Group to meet market expectations.

The Company is confident that this is a temporary delay …… albeit that they will fall outside of the current financial period. As a result, the Company's performance for FY24/25 will be materially below current consensus expectations.

The Group order book …… of £85.5m provides confidence that current earnings guidance for this year and next is deliverable, with potential to outperform, especially in view of spending on individually large programmes that are currently in abeyance.

The Directors are expecting to report revenues and adjusted profit before tax for FY 24/25 of at least £124 million and £4.25 million respectively, each ahead of consensus expectations. …… The Group re-iterates market expectations for the current financial year.
The strong order book underpins management's confidence in meeting market expectations for FY25/26, returning to year-on-year growth in revenue and profitability.

The Group has started the second half with a solid open order book of £87.3m …… This reflects a strong trading position notwithstanding global geo-political risks and economic variables, giving the Directors further confidence in meeting expectations for the full year.

Whilst order intake was slower in H1 2025/26, pleasingly we have seen order intake recover strongly at the beginning of H2 and the Directors remain confident in meeting consensus market expectations for FY25/26.

This strong trading means revenue is expected to be ahead of consensus market expectations and not less than £150m and adjusted profit before tax will accordingly also be ahead of consensus market expectations for FY25/26.
The Group has had a good start to the new financial year with current trading in line with the Board's expectations, and we expect to exceed current market expectations for FY26/27.

…… a strong order book, continued demand across the Group's target markets, and improving visibility into future periods, provides the Board with confidence in the Group's prospects. …… the Board remains confident in meeting its expectations for the full year.
